request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Information:
Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Age: 76 years
Gender: Male

Hospital Course:
The patient presented with a metachronous cancer in the sigmoid colon during surveillance colonoscopy after a previous right hemicolectomy for adenocarcinoma of the colon. He had undergone a second laparotomy with revision of the anastomosis due to an anastomotic leak during the immediate postoperative period. During the first postoperative week, the patient developed an enterocutaneous fistula with primary wound failure.

After subsequent management for the non-surgical healing of the fistula for 10 months, the patient underwent an abdominal wall reconstruction with an inlay polypropylene/polyglactin 910 composite mesh that was fixed using polypropylene sutures. The patient remained asymptomatic for 16 months after the primary surgery, after which he was diagnosed with a sigmoid cancer during surveillance colonoscopy.

At surgery, the patient underwent subtotal colectomy with ileorectal anastomosis. Several loops of bowel were tightly adherent to the anterior abdominal wall. After separating the loops from the posterior rectus sheath, an enterotomy was made to extract the heavily deposited mesh from inside the bowel lumen. There were no signs of an abscess, fistula, or sinus formation in the surrounding area.

Post-surgery, the patient had an uneventful recovery and was discharged in a stable condition.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
- Subtotal colectomy with ileorectal anastomosis
- Abdominal wall reconstruction with polypropylene/polyglactin 910 composite mesh

Condition at discharge:
The patient was discharged in a stable condition.

Follow-up plan:
The patient is advised to continue with follow-up colonoscopies as part of his surveillance protocol.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The episode in question is the admission for subtotal colectomy, performed for a metachronous sigmoid colon cancer found on surveillance colonoscopy. The principal diagnosis is therefore the malignant neoplasm of the sigmoid colon, which falls under C18 (malignant neoplasm of colon). The sigmoid colon is C18.7.

Other candidates were considered. The mesh found inside the bowel lumen (a mesh migration complication) was an incidental finding at surgery, not the reason for admission. A previous colon cancer would be a history code (Z85), but this is a new primary tumour under active treatment, so C18 applies.

CODE: C18
